headlines.text: On this day in 2021, there was a changing of the guard for the AEW World Tag Team Titles as The Lucha Brothers vs. The Young Bucks battled it out in a Steel Cage match, appearing on All Out, rated 9.49 ? the kind of match that redefines a wrestler's career ? ending the champion's reign at 10 defenses. A five-star classic inside a steel cage ? the Lucha Brothers entered to their theme song performed live for the first time, and delivered a war good enough to earn a perfect rating, dethroning the champions to capture their first AEW World Tag Team Titles.

Flash back to 2020, when there was a changing of the guard for the AEW World Tag Team Titles as FTR vs. Omega & Page battled it out, appearing on All Out, rated 7.73 ? a well-worked match ? ending the champion's reign at 7 defenses. For FTR, it marked a first real shot at championship gold. A changing of the guard in the tag division ? FTR, fresh off leaving WWE earlier that year, dethroned the reigning champions in a near-30-minute battle to capture their first AEW gold.
On a Friday in 2025, back when Konosuke Takeshita vs. Mark Briscoe headlined Collision, rated 8.02 ? a genuinely great match in a hard-fought men's division clash.

secondaries.text: On a Saturday in 2026, back when Alex Shelley stepped back through the curtain after a long-awaited absence after 4 years away, appearing on Collision.

Flash back to 2021, when Kenny Omega vs. Christian Cage went to battle over the AEW World Heavyweight Title, appearing on All Out, rated 8.16 ? a real highlight of the night. A hard-fought main event capping a stacked night that also saw three separate AEW debuts (Ruby Soho, Adam Cole, and Bryan Danielson) ? Omega successfully defended his title in a match many called one of the best of the entire show.

On this day in 2021, Miro vs. Eddie Kingston went to battle over the AEW TNT Title, appearing on All Out, rated 7.55 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle. This stood as the 30th match in AEW TNT Title history ? a real landmark for that championship. The opening match of a show many later called an all-timer ? Miro successfully defended the TNT Title in a hard-hitting contest that set the tone for one of AEW's most stacked pay-per-view cards ever.
